wins.title: Drafting tax memos in minutes
wins.summary: From function conversions to India-jurisdiction analysis — AI is replacing days-of-advisor turnaround with same-session output, often verified clean.
examples: Function-conversion memo drafted in 30 min (50K EUR advisor replaced, GDPR covered)
Premium Co-Pilot drafted an India memo; local expert confirmed it correct
AI drafted constructive feedback on a colleague's presentation
Agent answered a 2025 transfer-pricing court case in 2 minutes once company data was shared

wins.title: Financial modelling on autopilot
wins.summary: Models built from a prompt — change one variable and the agent reflows the rest, including entry/exit multiples.
examples: Change a variable, AI adjusts the rest; accurate across markets
One- and two-pager models from scratch via prompt; tax-rate change → multiples adjust automatically
Used AI to crunch complex financial computations

wins.title: ERP & data-extraction agents
wins.summary: Tax teams hooking AI into WorkDay, SAP, Slack and Alteryx to surface data without hunting through screens.
examples: Ask AI for ERP t-codes to look data up fast
Custom-built WorkDay ChatBot for t-codes, data extraction and dashboards
Slack → WorkDay generic data extraction (no salary fields)
SAP-extraction AI that infers the output before you specify requirements
Alteryx for data analysis and pattern recognition

wins.title: Catching up on emails & meetings
wins.summary: Co-Pilot triaging the inbox and capturing meeting argument structure we've been losing hours to.
examples: Co-Pilot summarises hundreds of daily email chains and pulls highlights
Co-Pilot prompt to capture argumental relationships and details in meetings

wins.title: Personal AI as productivity multiplier
wins.summary: Outside work licences, people are running AI on their own data — tax returns, translation, day-to-day decisions.
examples: Grok linked to Gmail/payslips/passport files country-specific tax returns end-to-end (saves half a day)
Dutch ↔ English voice translation live at an NOB meeting
Claude as translator on a trip in Japan
AI agents used to file personal tax returns
Claude for Instagram captions
ChatGPT to pick the best ice cream for breakfast
Claude Code built this whole dashboard last night

wins.title: AI as personal trainer
wins.summary: Letting the agent set your learning curriculum and decide when to dive deeper.
examples: 30-day study plan; daily readings + quizzes; AI decides when to go deeper

risks.title: Trust & hallucination
risks.summary: AI is inventing facts, breaking formulas and producing questionable methodologies. Every output needs a human re-read.
examples: Co-Pilot's meeting capture invented "data" from a conversation that never happened
AI calculations aren't always accurate, methodology can be questionable
AI-generated data-model formulas can quietly break

risks.title: Cost & licence economics
risks.summary: Tokens add up. External knowledge license is 3K EUR / month. Inhouse teams struggle to get 300 EUR fees approved. The KPI doesn't always justify the spend — and Group IT is policing usage.
examples: External knowledge licence — ~3,000 EUR / month for 5 users
Some companies won't even approve a 300 EUR AI budget
Every call burns tokens; humans still cheaper, KPIs don't always justify the data-centre cost
Group IT calls to police licence usage and threatens to pull the licence if not "maxed out"

risks.title: Quality ceiling on output
risks.summary: Cyber-security policies, mid-tier licences and conservative defaults are throttling how deep the AI is allowed to go.
examples: Co-Pilot's answers can sometimes feel less analytical than expected
Company cyber-security policies throttle Co-Pilot/ChatGPT analytical depth
AI replies can sound superficial — people can tell it wasn't the in-house advisor
AI-generated Instagram captions aren't human enough

risks.title: Advisor identity & accountability
risks.summary: If the agent does the technical advisory, what's the in-house advisor's value-add? And when the practitioner ships an unchecked AI mistake, leadership blames the human.
examples: If an agent does the technical work better, what's the in-house tax advisor's value-add now?
Communication stops feeling genuine when AI replies to colleagues on your behalf
Leadership will blame the practitioner if an AI mistake slips through unchecked

insights.title: AI is a tool, not an oracle
insights.summary: Don't expect it to be perfect — that's a bias we wouldn't apply to a human advisor. Take small wins first; criticise and disclaim freely.
examples: Don't expect AI to be perfect — we wouldn't apply that to a human advisor
Take small wins first — don't try to use AI in the most elaborate way from day one
Nothing wrong with criticising AI — disclaimers should be put on the output

insights.title: Humans stay in the loop
insights.summary: If AI learns from human input, the humans don't disappear — we just become the verifier and the teacher.
examples: "We have to be human to use AI."
If AI is trained on human input, how do we keep advancing it once humans plateau?

insights.title: Governance is coming
insights.summary: Audit standards and internal responsible-use rules are arriving — companies are already drafting them.
examples: There could (and maybe should) be an audit standard for AI use in tax computation
Some companies are starting to publish internal AI standards for responsible use

insights.title: Talent ↔ agent training loop
insights.summary: Agents train your talents, and your talents train the agents back — including the trick of asking AI to write its own prompts.
examples: AI agents can train your talents — and your talents can train the agents — inside the organisation
Ask AI to write the prompt for you, then feed it back to get the best result
We still need to learn to write very precise prompts to get good memos

insights.title: Market shifts in AI procurement
insights.summary: Multinationals are bypassing advisors by embedding tax databases directly — and Co-Pilot's price tiers determine how capable your team gets.
examples: Multinationals are looking to embed external tax databases directly into their own systems
Co-Pilot has different licences — the more you pay, the more sophisticated the model
AI is developing fast — one day mistakes will be fewer than humans'
